question.text: Within how many days after the AGM must a company identify unclaimed amounts and upload details on the company and IEPF websites in Form IEPF-2?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says companies must, within 60 days after their AGM (or the due date of the AGM where the AGM has not been held), identify unclaimed amounts and upload the relevant statement through Form IEPF-2. That directly supports option A. The Trap: The 30-day option (C) corresponds to the workbook timeline for crediting shares to the IEPF demat account, which is a separate requirement and not the Form IEPF-2 filing deadline. The 45-day option (B) corresponds to the grievance redressal timeline under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 and applies to intermediary grievances rather than IEPF filings. The 90-day option (D) does not match either of the source-backed figures. Note: The workbook lays out three distinct timelines that are easy to mix up: 60 days after the AGM for Form IEPF-2 upload, 30 days for credit of shares to the IEPF demat account once they become due for transfer, and 45 days for intermediary grievance redressal under the Intermediaries Regulations.
